# `liber:spool@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:spool` package (`spool.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem spooling - printers, and print jobs an application stages and explicitly submits, with an honest account of what the transport took.  A JOB IS A CAPABILITY, NOT AN ENDPOINT. `create` reserves the declared length and answers a job channel; the application writes exactly that many bytes, then `submit`s - and only then is anything eligible to reach the printer. Closing a job that was never submitted aborts it and refunds its reservation; closing a submitted one only stops watching it. Nothing on either interface reaches a catalogue, a backend, a reset or a raw endpoint.  `TRANSFERRED` MEANS THE TRANSPORT ACKNOWLEDGED EVERY BYTE, and nothing more: not a finished page. A job that ended any other way says why, how many bytes were confirmed, and whether more may have reached the printer than was confirmed. Nothing is ever replayed - not to the same printer, and not to a replacement.

## Interfaces

### interface `spool`

PRINTERS AND JOB CREATION. At most two live jobs per connection, and a job's whole declared length is reserved before it is admitted.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `printers` | `printers() -> result<list<printer-info>, error>` |  |
| 2 | `create` | `create(printer: printer-id, language: document-language, length: u32) -> result<handle<channel>, error>` |  |

### interface `job`

ONE JOB. `write` accepts a whole frame into the job's reservation or none of it; `submit` makes the staged bytes eligible for transmission exactly once; `status` stays available after submission.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `write` | `write(bytes: list<u8>) -> result<u32, error>` |  |
| 2 | `submit` | `submit() -> result<job-status, error>` |  |
| 3 | `status` | `status() -> result<job-status, error>` |  |
| 4 | `cancel` | `cancel() -> result<job-status, error>` |  |
